mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn can cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the cases when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases when UNRATE decreases by >0.5% over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the cases when HOUST increases over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases when INDPRO decreases by >1% over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) indicates a shift towards a more accommodative monetary policy and increased consumer savings, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% and RSAFS increases by >5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the cases when FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% and RSAFS increases by >5% over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.5% and UNRATE decreases by >0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the cases when PAYEMS increases by >0.5% and UNRATE decreases by >0.3% over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates growing economic demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the cases when GDPC1 increases over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >1% and CPIAUCSL increases by >2% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the cases when INDPRO decreases by >1% and CPIAUCSL increases by >2% over a 3-year period.
